story.title: The Web in the Kyoto Mists

sentences.text: My grandfather always walked these damp valley paths alone when the autumn chill settled in.
sentences.speaker: narrator

sentences.text: The sky turned blood red at dusk and hundreds of crows gathered above the old shrine.
sentences.speaker: narrator

sentences.text: According to old Kyoto legends, this was the exact sign that the great earth spider wakened.
sentences.speaker: narrator

sentences.text: It never walks, but glides a hand width above the ground with no sound and no wind.
sentences.speaker: narrator

sentences.text: The creature possessed a charcoal body with four glowing red eyes and thick bristling legs.
sentences.speaker: narrator

sentences.text: Each night it changed one small detail, and the grandfather clock in the hall ran backwards.
sentences.speaker: narrator

sentences.text: He reached his wooden gate and whispered a quiet plea into the dark.
sentences.speaker: narrator

sentences.text: Let me inside before it finds me.
sentences.speaker: person

sentences.text: A sudden shadow lunged from the eaves in a frantic blur of motion.
sentences.speaker: narrator

sentences.text: Only a dropped lantern remained smoking on the cobblestones.
sentences.speaker: narrator

sentences.text: Would you keep walking if your grandfather clock started running backwards?
sentences.speaker: narrator
